title: Black and Blue's objection to her Montreux festival appearance
summary: At Montreux in 1974 the Black and Blue people objected and brought an attorney, though Humes said she had no contract and would not sing her Black and Blue songs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: 1974, that's when you played the festival at Montreux?
And you had a little trouble with these people, Black and Blue, they didn't want you to . .
No, they said they didn't want me to because they said they recorded, they make records.
And they said, you on our records. So I said, I have no contract with you.

And he came and he didn't want me to do any of the songs that I had done for Black and Blue. I said, 'well I won't do that.' And so one of the first people I saw when I got to the festival was Nan and he had his attorney with him. He said, 'I brought my attorney'. I said, 'well you didn't need no attorney.' I said, 'I told you I wasn't going to do it. So that was all that mattered.' So he said, 'well we're going to see.' I said, 'well, you don't have to see'.
